newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea arrests ex-minister, MPs in loan scandal.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea arrests ex-minister, MPs in loan scandal.

text.p: South Korean prosecutors arrested a former cabinet minister and two lawmakers on Thursday over a loan scandal that has badly damaged the political credibility of President Kim Young-sam.
A prosecution official said Kim Woo-suk, who resigned on Wednesday as home affairs minister, was put behind bars on charges of accepting bribes from the failed Hanbo Steel Co.
"The former minister was accused of accepting money in return for a request to pressure officials to build a road to a Hanbo steel mill," he told Reuters.
The minister and one of the two arrested lawmakers, Hwang Byung-tai, are presidential loyalists belonging to a faction that backed Kim Young-sam's rise to power.
Hwang and the other lawmaker, Kwon Roh-kap, a top aide to opposition leader Kim Dae-jung, were also charged with bribery.

Earlier, a presidential spokesman said Prime Minister Lee Soo-sung offered to resign to carry the blame for the crisis, which was caused by one of South Korea's biggest bankruptcies and is turning into a political storm for the president.
"But President Kim turned down the offer, saying it was more important to resolve the crisis," the spokesman said.
Hanbo Steel, flagship of South Korea's 14th largest conglomerate, was declared insolvent on January 23 after piling up five trillion won ($5.8 billion) in loans.
Thursday's arrests bring to eight the number of people jailed in connection with the scandal, which deals a devastating blow to the president's image as an anti-corruption reformer.

On Tuesday, prosecutors arrested another veteran member of Kim's personal entourage, Hong In-gil, along with Chung Jae-chull, the highest-ranking official in the ruling New Korea Party after the president and the party chairman.
The others arrested are Hanbo Group founder Chung Tae-soo, and two leading bankers.
The prosecution official said prosecutors also sought to arrest a former Hanbo Group financier, Kim Jong-kook, on charges of embezzlement.
Senior prosecutor Choi Byung-koog told reporters that there were several other politicians suspected of involvement in the scandal.
"Kim Young-sam is facing the worst crisis of his political life," an editorial in the Chosun Ilbo daily said.
Kim took office in 1993 pledging to root out corruption from a country whose powerhouse economy was built on a murky alliance between politicians, big business and banks.

Kim cannot run for a second term, but with scandal swirling ever closer to him and his party's power centre, he will have less room to manoeuvre as he seeks to anoint a successor to run in December's elections.
The home affairs minister was the third cabinet member to depart under a corruption cloud in less than six months.
